Section(s): 2.4.2. Constant flow

Text and equations in reading order:
    When the flux rate is kept constant, the pressure increases as the membrane becomes fouled and Darcy's law reduces to Eq. (24)
(24) \frac{P}{P_{0}}=\frac{RA_{0}}{R_{0}A}    [code: algebraic, computes P, code proposes constitutive]
    The fouling will occur both by loss of area through the complete blocking mechanism, and by increased resistance due to caking on the membrane.
    Eq. (26) can be inserted into Eq. (27) to determine the resistance as a function of time. This equation and the equation for area as a function of time (9) can then be inserted into Eq. (24) to determine pressure as a function of time
(28) \frac{P}{P_{0}}=\frac{1}{(1-K_{\mathrm{b}}t)}\left(1-\frac{K_{\mathrm{c}}J_{0}^{2}}{K_{\mathrm{b}}}\ln(1-K_{\mathrm{b}}t)\right)    [code: algebraic, computes P, code proposes constitutive]
    This equation reduces to the equation for complete blocking when $ K_{c} $ is small and reduces to the equation for cake filtration when $ K_{b} $ is small. This equation will fit data where the pressure increases steeply and data where the pressure increases gradually, depending on the values of the fitted parameters. It will be more useful than models that can be made by combining the standard blocking equation with either the complete blocking model or the intermediate blocking model.
    For the combined cake-standard blocking model, the resistance increases over the course of the run and the membrane area remain constant. The pressure can be calculated as a function of time using Eq. (29)
(29) \frac{P}{P_{0}}=\left(\left(1-\frac{K_{\mathrm{s}}J_{0}t}{2}\right)^{-2}+K_{\mathrm{c}}J_{0}^{2}t\right)    [code: algebraic, computes P, code proposes constitutive]
    Eq. (30) allows calculation of pressure as a function of time using the combined intermediate blocking-cake filtration model
(30) \frac{P}{P_{0}}=\exp(K_{\mathrm{i}}J_{0}t)\left(1+\frac{K_{\mathrm{c}}J_{0}}{K_{\mathrm{i}}}(\exp(K_{\mathrm{i}}J_{0}t)-1)\right)    [code: algebraic, computes P, code proposes constitutive]
    Table 1 Summary of the five constant pressure combined fouling models
    Pressure as a function of time in the combined standard and complete blocking model will be described by Eq. (31)
(31) \frac{P}{P_{0}}=\frac{1}{(1-K_{\mathrm{b}}t)\Big(1+\frac{K_{\mathrm{s}}J_{0}}{2K_{\mathrm{b}}}\ln(1-K_{\mathrm{b}}t)\Big)^{2}}    [code: algebraic, computes P, code proposes constitutive]
    Pressure as a function of time in the combined standard and intermediate blocking model will be described by Eq. (32)
(32) \frac{P}{P_{0}}=\frac{\exp(K_{\mathrm{i}}J_{0}t)}{\left(1-\frac{K_{\mathrm{s}}}{2K_{\mathrm{i}}}(\exp(K_{\mathrm{i}}J_{0}t)-1)\right)^{2}}    [code: algebraic, computes P, code proposes constitutive]
    The equations reduce to their respective component models at the limits where one fouling mode dominates. Eq. (29)–(32) will be applicable to the cases where the fouling is observed to occur by a specific combination of mechanisms. The equations however will not fit as wide a range of data as the combined cake-complete model and are therefore not as useful in general. A summary of the five new constant flow combined fouling models, including the names, component mechanisms, equations and fitted parameters is provided in Table 2.

Symbols:
  P: trans-membrane pressure [Pa] (computed)
  R: resistance to filtration [m^{-1}] (computed)
  A_{0}: initial membrane frontal area [m^{2}] (parameter)
  R_{0}: initial resistance to filtration [m^{-1}] (parameter)
  A: available membrane frontal area [m^2] (computed)
  P_{0}: initial reference pressure (variable)
  K_{b}: complete blocking constant [s^{-1}] (parameter)
  t: time [s] (variable)
  K_{c}: cake filtration constant [s/m^{2}] (parameter)
  J_{0}: initial flux [m/s] (variable)
  K_{s}: standard blocking constant [m^{-1}] (parameter)
  K_{i}: intermediate blocking constant [m^{-1}] (parameter)

Model-wide assumptions (already recorded, do not repeat):
  - Cake formation and complete pore blockage occur simultaneously.
  - Deposited aggregates are permeable.
  - Intermediate blocking assumes that a portion of the particles seal off pores and the rest accumulate on top of other deposited particles.
  - Standard blocking assumes that particles accumulate inside membranes on the walls of straight cylindrical pores.
  - Complete blocking assumes that particles seal off pore entrances and prevent flow.

Laws: 24, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32

laws.description: At constant flow, pressure relative to its reference value scales with filtration resistance and inversely with available membrane area.
